method: Independent re-fetch of every eazli.com source via WebFetch, checked against the claims this repo makes and the numbers hardcoded in app/main.py. The original capture (2026-08-06) was taken through a browser session; this pass confirms it from a different client so the grounding does not rest on a single scrape.
why: Every number this project quotes about eazli — the returns-reduction range, the plan quotas, the Fitment clause — is load-bearing. The teardown argues from them and app/main.py enforces them. A claim nobody re-checked is a claim that quietly rots.

confirms: Zeina — AI Guide. Verbatim: "She knows that the early stages of a home plan are usually a mess of tabs, screenshots, and 'maybes'. Zeina filters that noise." and that she "gives you a map" rather than a catalog or quote.
Adam — AI Sales Advisor (title only on this page).
Noura — AI Design Agent (title only on this page).
new_since_capture: Claims "68% Users find home decisions simpler and less stressful with an AI agent by their side" and "200k+ Real conversations every month". Not previously recorded.
The page states no limit on what any agent may do. The only published scope constraints live on /terms-ai-agent.

confirms: "27%-43% Reduction in returns driven by better fit, visualization & expectations" — the number the whole fit-checking thesis is aimed at.
"~19% Increase in average order value through smart bundles & guided upsell".
"~12% AI-assisted conversion rate vs. ~0.5-3% unassisted shopping".
new_since_capture: "~300% Conversion lift when buyers are guided by AI agents" — a fourth metric not previously recorded.
sources.note: Only the first vendor FAQ answer is present in fetched HTML; the other four render on expand. Independently reproduces the accordion behaviour the original capture had to use browser automation to get around.

confirms: 47 questions, matching the original capture's count exactly.
"How do the agents work together?" and "Will I need to manage multiple agents?" are both present — the questions that imply an orchestrator-with-specialists design.
"Are AI recommendations professional advice?" and "Does Eazli coordinate delivery and installation?" are present.
sources.note: A plain fetch returns questions with no answers, confirming the lazy-accordion rendering. The answers in kb/raw/faq.json remain the only capture of them and were taken through a browser.

confirms: Explorer: "Design 1 room with up to 5 layout options & 10 re-designs each month".
Active: "Design multiple rooms with 15 layout revisions and 20 re-designs each month", plus taste learning, custom furniture requests and price-drop alerts.
These match PLANS in app/main.py exactly: explorer {rooms 1, layouts 5, redesigns 10}, active {rooms 99, layouts 15, redesigns 20}.
sources.note: Prices render as ".../ year" with no figure. The quota numbers are what this project enforces, and those are published.

confirms: Named offerings: Home Essentials, Services & Design, AI Agents, Inspiration Hub.
Named AI tools: AI Room Decorator, AI Exterior Designer, **AI Floor Planner**.
sources.note: Still makes no claim anywhere about fit, measurement, delivery or installation — the gap this prototype is built into. Worth stating plainly: eazli already ships an 'AI Floor Planner', so the contribution here is not the idea of planning a room, it is refusing to assert a spatial fact the engine cannot verify.

sources.reason: A plain fetch returns only the footer and navigation; the body renders client-side.
sources.note: kb/raw/policy-ai-agent-scope.md holds the browser capture, and the two clauses this project leans on are present verbatim there: the Fitment clause ("You are responsible for verifying all site and access measurements (including doorways, hallways, stairs, and elevators). Eazli shall not be liable if an item (e.g., a sofa) cannot be delivered, moved in, installed, or used as intended...") and the Visualizations, Dimensions & Color disclaimer. Unverified by a second client, and labelled as such rather than assumed.

outcome: No claim in this repo was contradicted. Two metrics and one agent statistic were found that the original capture missed, and one page could not be re-fetched by a second client and is marked accordingly.
